title: Temperature, Humidity, and Environmental Conditions
summary: Compare environmental readings without treating scenario limits as universal rules.
objectives: Interpret inlet, exhaust, and humidity readings.
Explain why context and equipment requirements matter.

vocab.def: The amount of water vapor in air.
The location where air enters equipment.
A pattern of change across multiple readings.

sections.heading: Context matters
sections.body: Temperature and humidity affect equipment and the environment. Actual operating limits depend on equipment and facility requirements; classroom thresholds are scenario-specific operating limits.

sections.heading: Compare readings
sections.body: A single sensor value may not explain system condition. Compare locations, time, trends, and related evidence.

practice.prompt: Why should a classroom humidity limit not be presented as universal?
practice.answer: Actual limits depend on the equipment, facility, and documented operating context.

quiz.question: What is stronger than one isolated reading?
options: A contextual trend across relevant sensors
quiz.answer: A contextual trend across relevant sensors

reflectionPrompt: Which sensor comparison would reduce uncertainty?
